transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-18
Start: 16:00 UTC (08:00 PT)
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Claire (Redwood SE), Jared (CTO, Luminary), Priya (Head Eng), Leah (Security Manager), Tom (DevOps)

[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. I'm Samir from Redwood, AE on this account, with Claire our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:07] Jared: Good thanks, bit of a busy morning here. Thanks for fitting us in.
[00:10] Priya: Morning. We'll try to be concise, we have a tight window.
[00:14] Samir: Totally, we'll keep to the agenda: quick intro, your environment and constraints, security controls (SOC2, SSO, RBAC, KMS), and then next steps.
[00:23] Claire: Quick note — feel free to interrupt, I may jump into technical details.
[00:27] Leah: Perfect. From Luminary's side, I'll own the compliance questions.

[00:35] Samir: Great. Jared, can you give us a bit of background: what are you evaluating Redwood for and what are your must-haves?
[00:43] Jared: Sure. We're building an assistant inside our platform for customer support routing and internal knowledge. Latency matters but security matters more. We're evaluating hosted first, but likely will need Dedicated or Private because of our data residency and control requirements. Must-haves: SOC 2 Type II, customer key control, SSO integration with our Okta IdP, RBAC for multiple teams, and extensive audit logs with 7 year retention for certain records.
[01:05] Samir: Thanks. When you say "customer key control" are you looking for BYOK with an HSM-backed KMS?
[01:12] Leah: Yes, ideally customer-managed keys, key rotation policies, and we need to show chain-of-custody for keys in audits.
[01:18] Tom: Also note our infra is in AWS eu-west-1. Data residency requirement says inference must run in EU for EU customers.
[01:26] Claire: We support VPC deployments and can pin regions, including eu-west-1, for Redwood Private or Dedicated in an EU region. For Hosted, we can constrain routing but there are limitations — we'd want to discuss SLAs.

[01:40] Jared: Can you outline what lives where for each model — Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. We want to map responsibility for keys, logs, PII handling.
[01:49] Claire: Short version: Hosted is our public API — Redwood controls the control plane and key management by default; logs are stored in our infra with retention policies but we can offer managed options. Dedicated is reserved capacity in our managed infra where you have tenant isolation and network controls; for KMS, we can support customer KMS via cross-account access or you can provision a managed HSM — though there are setup steps. Private is a customer-managed control plane or on-prem cluster — here you retain the keys and full network isolation.
[02:19] Priya: Is the audit log format standardized? We need to ingest into our SIEM (Splunk).
[02:25] Claire: Yes we stream audit events; format is JSON with event types, request id, user identity, token usage, and model version. There are sometimes naming mismatches in auto-transcripts, but we can map fields. We commonly integrate via Kinesis or Kafka connectors or S3 delivering to your pipeline.

[02:45] Leah: Retention — we have strict regulatory needs. 7 years for certain transaction records, 1 year for others. Can Redwood guarantee retention for that duration?
[02:55] Samir: We can set retention windows on logs. Long-term cold storage of logs is typically an add-on; for Dedicated/Private, it's much simpler because you control the bucket or the retention. For Hosted, we can commit via contract but you won't have direct control of the underlying storage buckets.

[03:12] Tom: Regarding SSO, Okta is our IdP. Do you support SP-initiated and IdP-initiated SAML flows and SCIM for provisioning?
[03:20] Claire: Yes, we support SAML 2.0 SP and IdP flows, and SCIM for user provisioning. There are some edge cases with SCIM attributes mapping if you have custom attributes. We usually do a short integration checklist and a staging test.
[03:34] Jared: RBAC — we need least-privilege: developers should be able to run test jobs, but not access production prompt datasets; support needs read-only logs. How granular is RBAC?
[03:44] Claire: RBAC is role-based with resources and actions mapping. You can scope to token-level, model-level, and route-level. For Private deployments you can plug into your own IAM, otherwise we provide fine-grained roles. We also support audit-level impersonation logs for service accounts.

[04:03] Priya: If we go Dedicated and there's a capacity issue, what happens? Will traffic rollover to your Hosted models? That's a concern for data exfil if it spills to shared tenants.
[04:13] Samir: Default policy is fail-open or fail-closed depending on config — but we implement strict non-fallback for customers that require no cross-tenant routing. For enterprise contracts we can ensure no cross-tenant fallbacks and instead queue requests or return 503s. For lower tiers, there's automated fallback to compatible variants. We'll need to document it.

[04:35] Leah: SOC2 evidence — can you share your latest Type II and the associated controls? Also, ISO 27001?
[04:43] Samir: Yes, we'll share our SOC 2 Type II report and ISO summary under NDA. Claire will attach the pen test summary as well.
[04:49] Leah: Do you store transcripts for debug by default? We want to make sure PII is redacted and have options to disable retention.
[04:56] Claire: By default we retain request/response for 30 days for debugging and quality; for enterprise we can configure retention and automatic PII redaction. For Private deployments you control retention and the storage lifecycle. There are options to disable logging of full-text responses and only keep metadata.

[05:14] Tom: For KMS, what's the pattern for BYOK? Do you do envelope encryption and do you support importing keys or strict HSMs?
[05:21] Claire: Envelope encryption is standard: the model runtime uses a data key encrypted with your KMS. We integrate with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and bring-your-own-HSM offerings via external key manager (EKM). There are some additional compliance steps but it's supported.

[05:36] Jared: How about multi-region replication — we need EU-only processing for EU customers but US for US customers.
[05:42] Samir: We can route requests by customer attribute and pin model hosting to region-specific capacity. For Dedicated we can allocate pools in eu-west-1 and us-east-1 and route accordingly. For Hosted, we can set routing preferences but absolute guarantees are part of enterprise contract terms.

[06:00] Priya: Does Redwood support token-level cost and latency traces so we can compute unit economics?
[06:07] Claire: Yes our Console exposes token breakdown, latency percentiles, and per-route cost. You can export trace data to your observability stack.

[06:15] Jared: Ok, a few follow-ups: we will be required to see encryption key custody proof, an architecture diagram showing network flows and where logs live, and a runbook for incident response.
[06:26] Leah: Also, how do you handle access reviews and SSO de-provisioning audit? We do quarterly attestations.
[06:33] Claire: SCIM de-provisioning events are logged and we can emit reports for attestation windows. For shared keys or service accounts we recommend short-lived tokens and automatic rotation.

[06:48] Tom: On the practical side, what does a pilot look like? We want a short benchmark that shows latencies at our typical sequence lengths and token mixes and a security review in parallel.
[06:58] Samir: We typically run a 1-week Dedicated trial: we provision reserved capacity in the region you choose, run your workloads and capture latency/cost traces. We'll lock down networking and audit controls so you can run your security assessments concurrently.

[07:15] Priya: Budget question — rough order of magnitude for a short Dedicated pilot and then a 6-month reserved capacity?
[07:22] Samir: Roughly, pilots are low-cost (engineering time plus a small infra deposit), and reserved capacity pricing depends on GPU type and commitment. I'll send a ballpark pricing sheet after the call.

[07:34] Jared: A nit — we saw references to "KV cache" optimizations on your site. Does that cache anything sensitive?
[07:41] Claire: KV cache is model internals for fast generation (keys/values in memory). It doesn't persist PII to disk in normal ops. For extra assurance, we can disable persistent caches and ensure ephemeral memory only. The transcript auto tool sometimes calls it K V cash which is amusing.

[07:57] Leah: Are there any third-party subprocessors that have access to raw request/response payloads?
[08:03] Samir: We list subprocessors in our DPA. For Hosted, some managed infastructure vendors have access to underlying storage for operational reasons; for Dedicated/Private, we minimize subprocessors and can provide a list. We'll share the subprocessor list and DPA link.

[08:18] Priya: We need a timeline. We're hoping to select a vendor by end of April and run a pilot mid-May. Feasible?
[08:26] Samir: Feasible. Immediate steps: share artifacts, schedule the pilot kickoff, and a technical deep-dive on SSO/KMS.

[08:36] Claire: I'll put together a deployment checklist: network ports, VPC peering, allowed IP ranges, and KMS integration steps.

[08:42] Jared: For legal, our counsel will want to see data residency clauses and SLAs around availability and fallbacks.
[08:49] Samir: We'll loop in our contracts team and share template terms.

[08:55] Leah: Quick question about log retention encryption at rest — is that encrypted with our key if we provide KMS?
[09:01] Claire: For Dedicated/Private yes, you control the encryption. For Hosted we can support customer-managed keys for certain artifacts via envelope encryption; there are design constraints but it's possible.

[09:13] Tom: Ok, sounds like we have alignment on major items. Any blockers from Redwood's side?
[09:19] Samir: None immediate. We'll need NDA/scoped SOC 2 sharing and your minimal test dataset. We'll also need a point of contact for network access and a security champion to run through the checklist.

[09:32] Jared: Leah will be lead for security, Tom for infra, Priya for engineering integration.

[09:38] Samir: Great. Let's recap next steps: we'll email SOC 2 and pen test docs; Claire will share deployment diagram and checklist; Luminary will assemble test data and requirements doc; schedule pilot kickoff for week of 2026-03-30.

[09:54] Priya: One last clarifying point — when you say "no cross-tenant fallback" in Dedicated, will that affect latency or availability in ways we should test?
[10:02] Claire: It could increase visibility into capacity constraints (e.g., queueing). We'll run scenarios in the pilot so you can evaluate trade-offs.

[10:11] Jared: Sounds good. Thanks both. We'll expect the docs and to schedule the deep dive next week.

[10:18] Samir: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with a single email summarizing action items and links.
[10:22] Leah: Thanks.

End of call.

Call artifacts referenced during meeting:
- Redwood SOC 2 Type II (will be shared under NDA)
- Penetration test executive summary (Claire to attach)
- Deployment checklist (Claire to produce)
- Pilot test plan template (Samir to share)

Recap (verbatim from meeting close):
Samir: "We'll send SOC2, pen test, deployment diagram — Luminary to provide data and we'll kick off a Dedicated pilot week of March 30th."

Notes on transcript quality: auto-transcription changed some product names (e.g., "KV cache" -> "K V cash", "Dedicated" once as "Dedicaited"). Some speaker labels merged in places.
